images.title: Six products, two pairs of like terms
images.purpose: Shows the six products of (a + b)(a² + 2ab + b²) and how the two pairs of like terms combine.
images.composition: One row of six rounded tiles across the middle, with two brackets underneath joining the like terms. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Six equal rounded rectangle tiles in one horizontal row, in this order: 'a³' (white with dark outline), 'a²b' (amber #E69F00), '2a²b' (amber), '2ab²' (green #009E73), 'ab²' (green), 'b³' (white with dark outline). Under the two amber tiles, one thin grey bracket joins them to the label '3a²b' below. Under the two green tiles, one thin grey bracket joins them to the label '3ab²' below. Exactly 6 tiles, 2 brackets.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: After multiplying out, add only the like terms: a²b with 2a²b, ab² with 2ab².
images.description: Shows the six products of (a + b)(a² + 2ab + b²) and how the two pairs of like terms combine.
images.context: (a + b)(a² + 2ab + b²) = a³ + 3a²b + 3ab² + b³; check a = 1, b = 2 gives 27.

image_decisions.why: Collecting like terms is a sorting idea; colour matching makes the two pairs visible.
